Technical 
 Procedure
Title

Total 
 Dissolved Soilds Dried at 180oC

Using Standard Method for the Examination 
 of

Waterand 
 WasteWater18th Edition, Method 2540 C ( 
 Gravimetric, Dried at 180C )
Introduction

This 
method is used to determine the dissolved salts (solids) for drinking water, surface, and saline water, waste water and industrial water and by this 
method one can classify water and determine if water is suitable to be used for 
public health purposes.

The first 
draft was initiated by Chemist/ Amal Ali Shalaby reviewed by chemical general 
director / Aness Abu Al EZZ, revised by quality control Chemist/ Wael A. 
Tantawy and accepted by Eng/ Mohamed Hamouda Al sarrag the Head Sector of Damiatta 
Power Station.

This document accepted by eng.
 Samir Abdel Gilel: EDEPC MPIS coordinator & 
 inspection and 
 quality control general director, and certified by 
 accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman EDEPC admin. & financial inspection, 
 quality control general director and supervisor of inspection & quality 
 control head sector.
Summary of Method

The solution of total matter is to be filtered 
 through a standard glass fiber filter to isolate the particulate 
 matter, then the solution of dissolved matter is evaporated to dryness till we 
 have a constant weight at 180C.
Interference

Highly mineralized waters containing significant 
concentrations of calcium, magnesium chloride and / or sulfate may be hygroscopic 
and will require prolonged drying, desiccation and rapid weighing.

Samples containing high concentrations of 
bicarbonate will require careful and possibly prolonged drying at 180C to 
insure that all the bicarbonate is converted to carbonate.
Safety Precautions

Reagent grade chemicals shall be used in all tests or it must of sufficiently 
high purity.

Collect the sample 
 in accordance with the applicable Method of 
 Document Water-004-r0.
Rapid weighing of ignited residues because of possible moisture absorption.

There is likelihood of interference from carbonates, organic matter, nitrate and 
nitrate nitrogen water hydration, chlorides, and sulfates which may be 
decomposed either completely or in part when ignited 
at 600oC 
(1112oF).

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment
Apparatus

Glass Fiber Filter Disc- 4.7cm 
or 2.1cm, without organic binder. Reeve Angel type 934 AH, Gelman type A / E, 
or equivalent.

Filter 
Holder- Membrane filter funnel or Gooch crucible adapter.
Suction Flask- 500 ml.

Gooch Crucibles- 
25 ml ( if 2.1 cm filter is used ).

Evaporation Dishes- Porcelain,100 ml volume.( Vycor or platinum dishes may be 
substituted ).
Steam Bath.

Drying Oven- 
 For operation at 180oC 2oC.
Desiccators.
Analytical balance- Capable of weighing to 0.1 mg,
Reagents
Distilled water.
Work to be Carried out

Preparation of Glass Fiber Filter Disc:
Place the disc on the membrane filter apparatus or insert into bottom of a 
suitable Gooch crucible. While vacuum is applied, wash the disc with three 
successive 20 ml volumes of distilled water. Remove all traces of water by 
continuing to apply vacuum after water has passed through. Discard washings.

Preparation of Evaporating Dishes:
When filterable residue is to be measured heat the clean dish to 180 
 2oC for one hour cool in desiccator and store until needed. 
Weigh immediately before use.

Assemble the filtering apparatus and begin suction. Shake the sample vigorously 
and rapidly transfer 100 ml to the funnel by means of a 100 ml graduated 
cylinder. If total filterable residue is low, a larger volume may be filtered.

Filter the sample through the glass fiber filter, rinse with three 10 ml 
portions of distilled water and continue to apply vacuum for about 3 minutes 
after filtration is complete to remove as much water as possible.

Transfer 100 ml (or a larger volume) of the filtrate to a weighed evaporating 
dish and evaporate to dryness on a steam bath.

Dry the evaporated sample for at least one hour at 180 
 2oC. Cool in a desiccator and weigh. Repeat the drying cycle 
until a constant weight is obtained or until weight loss is less than 0.5 mg.
